DEEP SEA CREATURE FILE / SNAILFISH

LIFE UNDER EXTREME PRESSURE

Hadal Snailfish

Hadal snailfish are adapted to life in some of the deepest ocean trenches, where water pressure is immense, temperatures are low and sunlight never reaches. Their soft, flexible bodies and specialised biology help them survive these conditions.

Survival & behaviour

Rather than relying on heavy armour, snailfish have bodies suited to deep-water life. They feed on small animals living near the seafloor, including tiny crustaceans. Different snailfish species occupy different depths.

Creature facts

HabitatDeep ocean trenches, including hadal depths
BodySoft and flexible
DietSmall crustaceans and other tiny seafloor animals
ChallengesCold, darkness and enormous pressure
DEEP-SEA FACTSnailfish have been observed at extraordinary depths, making them among the deepest-living fish known. Their adaptations to pressure, cold and darkness are highly specialised.
